newsitem.title: UK: UK Labour says very difficult to defeat government.
newsitem.headline: UK Labour says very difficult to defeat government.

text.p: John Prescott, deputy leader of Britain's opposition Labour party, said it would be very difficult to unseat the Conservative government even though it was now in a minority after losing the Wirral South by-election.
"If the Ulster Unionists have made clear, as indeed they have, that they intend to vote for the government...it will be very difficult to defeat the government," he told BBC radio.
"We can harass and harry them. What we can't complete is a confidence motion if the other political parties don't join with us."
Prescott said Labour would not be prepared to put down a confidence motion unless it could hope to win it.
But Labour would not simply sit back and wait for May 1, believed to be Prime Minister John Major's favoured date for an election, and would continue to conduct a very vigorous opposition, he added.
